title: PERCEPTION DETERMINES REALITY
subtitle: Selective Disclosure, Redaction, and Context-Sufficiency Provenance Extension

new_primitives.DISCLOSURE_ROOT: Authenticated commitment to a canonical structured source object.
new_primitives.SELECTIVE_DISCLOSURE_PROOF: Proof that a disclosed field/claim belongs to DISCLOSURE_ROOT without revealing all hidden content.
new_primitives.REDACTION_MANIFEST: Derivative metadata describing disclosed paths, hidden context policy and proof set.

core_rule: Selective disclosure may prove source membership without proving complete context, current authority or semantic sufficiency.
structured_commitment_contract: canonical source fields/claims have stable paths and encodings
the commitment root is bound inside the portable provenance envelope
disclosed leaves are accompanied by membership proofs
hidden leaf contents are not required merely to prove disclosed membership
redacted output receives a derivative claim identity
context_rule: A verifier must separately evaluate whether omitted context could change the meaning, scope, negation, conditions or authority of the disclosed fragment.
authority_rule: If redaction removes fields necessary for current authority epoch, scope, revocation or qualifier checks, the object cannot retain executable authority even when disclosed content membership verifies.
privacy_rule: Reveal the minimum provenance needed for the receiving decision; provenance should support privacy rather than require wholesale disclosure.
verification_requirements: prove one public claim belongs to a committed source while a private field stays hidden
tamper disclosed field and reject membership proof
hide negating or qualifying context and mark CONTEXT_SUFFICIENCY=INSUFFICIENT
hide authority fields and downgrade executable authority
treat screenshot of redacted view as display evidence unless underlying selective proof is independently verified
canonical_lines: Membership in a source is not completeness of context.
Privacy can hide content without severing provenance.
A redacted object may prove where it came from while still lacking enough information to authorize action.
